pages.title: Temporary restaurants: what you need to know
pages.description: What counts as a temporary restaurant in Barbados, who must apply for a permit, and what your event needs — including food safety, paying for Environmental Health Officers, and setting up your stall.
pages.body_markdown:
This page explains the rules for temporary restaurants — who needs a permit, what it costs and what to have ready. It covers [applying for a temporary restaurant permit](/business-trade/apply-for-temporary-restaurant-permit) and [requesting an environmental health officer](/business-trade/request-an-environmental-health-officer).

## What counts as a temporary restaurant

A **temporary restaurant** is a food stall, booth, tent, table, bar or any similar setup where food or drinks are prepared or served to the public for up to 30 days.

**Food** means anything people eat or drink. This includes meals, snacks, sweets, cut fruit, drinks and chewing gum, as well as anything used to make or prepare food. It does not include cosmetics, tobacco or anything used only as medicine. This applies even if food is not your main business.

**See the legal definitions**

In law, a temporary restaurant is “a restaurant which operates for a period not exceeding 30 days” (Health Services (Restaurants) Regulations, 1969).

In law, food is “any substance, whether processed, semi-processed or raw, which is intended for human consumption and includes drink, chewing gum and other substances which are used in the manufacture or treatment of food, but does not include cosmetics, tobacco or substances used only as drugs” (Health Services (Food Hygiene) Regulations, 1969).

You need a permit if you will serve or offer for sale, any food or drink, whether carried on for profit or not. This also includes **bars, snacks** and **confectioneries**, **free samples or product promotions**.

[Apply for a permit](/business-trade/apply-for-temporary-restaurant-permit)

## Who needs to apply

Both the event organiser and each food vendor must apply. If you are a vendor, make your own application for each stall you will operate.

If your event is likely to draw large crowds, the Environmental Health Department will assign officers to it.

If someone else is organising the event, ask them for a letter confirming they have given you permission to operate. You will need to upload it with your application.

Apply at least **14 days** before the event.

## Before the event

-   Everyone handling food must get a valid medical certificate, and have it during the event.
-   To obtain a medical certificate in Barbados, you can visit a private doctor, private clinic or public polyclinic.
-   Your permit will be issued at the event by the Environmental Health Officer, at the completion and successful compliance to the Environmental Health Department standards.
-   Keep your permit at your stall.
-   Some temporary permits may be granted by the Environmental Health Department based on a risk based assessment.

## Paying for Environmental Health Officers

There is no application fee. If you are organising the event and it falls outside normal working hours, you must pay any overtime costs for the officers allocated to the event by the Ministry of Health and Wellness. An invoice will be sent after you submit your application.

-   The overtime fees are **payable in advance**, to the Accountant General or the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Health and Wellness— do not make cheques payable to the polyclinic. This is set by regulation 7(2) of the Health Services (Assignment of Public Health Inspectors to Private Businesses) Regulations, 1986.
-   Pay at least 2 days before the event.
-   Pay by cash or cheque only. Make cheques payable to the Accountant General.
-   Take your payment with a copy of the invoice to the polyclinic or to the Environmental Health Department, Ministry of Health and Wellness, Frank Walcott Building, Culloden Road, St. Michael.
-   You will get a receipt.

[Request an environmental health officer](/business-trade/request-an-environmental-health-officer)

## What counts as a mass event

A mass event or mass gathering is generally defined as a large-scale public assembly that includes but not limited to: a festival, concert, sporting match, a fair, fete, wedding, breakfast party or a j'ouvert —where a high concentration of people strains health and sanitation resources, triggering special response from the Environmental Health Department, issuing of temporary restaurant permits and strict food safety protocols.

## Setting up your stall

Your stall must meet food-safety standards for construction.

Your stall must have:

-   A roof and at least **3 sides**, built from smooth, clean, easy-to-clean materials.
-   Flooring that is smooth, clean and sloped for drainage.
-   Food kept **at least 18 inches off the ground**, covered or behind sneeze guards.
-   A handwashing station — a container of **at least 20 litres** with a tap, liquid soap and paper towels.
-   Separate basins for washing hands and washing utensils, and a container for waste water.
-   Equipment to keep hot food hot (60°C or above) and cold food cold (5°C or below).
-   A covered, leak-proof bin for waste, and a supply of safe water.

A **site or stall plan** is a simple drawing of your event layout. It should show where each stall will be, and where you will put handwashing stations, water, waste bins and toilets. If you are organising the event, upload it with your application — for a single stall, a hand-drawn sketch is fine.

## Keeping food safe

Officers check that food is kept safe. The basics are:

-   Keep cold food at **5°C or below**, and hot food at **60°C or above**.
-   Cook food thoroughly — to at least **70°C** — especially meat, poultry, eggs and seafood.
-   Do not leave food that can spoil at room temperature for more than **2 hours**.
-   Keep raw and ready-to-eat food separate, with separate utensils and cutting boards, and store food in covered containers.
-   Keep food and containers **off the ground** at all times, and keep stored food well covered.
-   Wash and sanitise all surfaces and equipment, and protect food from insects, pests and other animals.
-   Wash fruit and vegetables, and do not use food beyond its expiry date.
-   Do not thaw food at room temperature, and reheat cooked food thoroughly.
-   Use safe water, wash your hands often, and keep hair covered.
-   Do not handle food if you are unwell.

## Personal hygiene for food handlers

Everyone handling food must follow these rules on the day. An officer will check them during the inspection.

### What to wear

-   Cover your hair with a **hairnet**. Anyone with a beard must also wear a **beard net**.
-   Wear **clean clothes and an apron**. Keep your arms and shoulders covered — officers do not accept sleeveless tops.
-   Do not wear **jewellery** — earrings, necklaces, chains, wristwatches, rings or bracelets.
-   Keep your **nails** short, clean and unvarnished. Do not wear false nails.
-   Do not wear **make-up**, **perfume or cologne**, or **false eyelashes**.
-   Do not wear clothing with **outer pockets**, or carry items in your pockets.

### Keeping yourself clean

-   Wash your hands regularly and properly, and always after using the toilet.
-   Cover every cut or wound with a **waterproof dressing**.
-   Use tongs or spoons to handle ready-to-eat food. Do not handle it with bare hands.
-   Stay away if you are unwell — vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or a sore throat.

### What not to do at the stall

-   Do not cough, sneeze or talk over food.
-   Do not eat, drink, smoke or chew gum in food areas.
-   Do not handle **money and food** at the same time.
-   Do not use a **mobile phone** in food preparation areas.

## Contact us

You do not need to choose a polyclinic. When you apply, your application will be directed to the appropriate polyclinic based on the event location and shown to you before you submit. If you are unsure, you can call the Ministry to check.

**Ministry of Health and Wellness**

-   Telephone: [1 (246) 536-3800](tel:+12465363800)
-   Email: [info@health.gov.bb](mailto:info@health.gov.bb)
-   Frank Walcott Building, Culloden Road, St. Michael

pages.title: Apply for a school uniform grant
pages.description: Apply for a $100 grant towards your child’s school uniform for a Barbadian primary school.
pages.body_markdown: If your child is starting or continuing at a Barbadian primary school for the new school year, you can apply for a $100 grant towards the cost of their school uniform. You can claim one grant per child each school year, paid into your bank or credit union account. ## Who can apply You can apply if your child is enrolled at a Barbadian primary school for the current or upcoming school year. You can claim one grant per child per school year, and you can only apply once for each child in that year. ## How to apply You can apply online. It takes about 10 minutes. Start now ## What the form asks for You’ll need to give: 1. Your details as the parent or guardian — your name, National ID number, home address, parish, mobile number and email address. 2. Your child’s details — their full name, date of birth, school, school year and class level. 3. Your bank or credit union account details so the grant can be paid. You’ll also need to confirm that your information is true and correct, and that you have not already applied for this grant for this child this school year. ## After you apply The Ministry of Educational Transformation will check your child’s enrolment with their school. Once your application is approved, the $100 grant is paid into your account within 4 weeks. You’ll get a confirmation email and a reference number you can use to track your application. If you have not heard anything within 4 weeks, you can call +1 (246) 535-0700 or email grants@mes.gov.bb.

pages.title: Apply for a sixth form placement
pages.description: Apply for placement in a public secondary school that offers Sixth Form (CAPE) study.
pages.body_markdown: If you have completed CSEC and want to continue your studies at a public secondary school that offers Sixth Form (CAPE), use this service to apply. There is no application fee. ## Who can apply You can apply if you have completed CSEC examinations and want a Sixth Form placement at a public secondary school that offers CAPE. Placement is not guaranteed. It depends on the availability of spaces and the entry requirements of each school. Each school sets its own minimum grades for each subject — typically at least 5 CSEC passes (Grades I, II or III) including English A and Mathematics. If you are waiting on your results, you can still apply by selecting ‘Pending’ as the grade. ## Before you start You will need documents ready to upload: 1. Your CSEC results slip or certificate. 2. Your birth certificate. 3. Your National ID, if you are 16 or over. Apply by the deadline announced by the Ministry — usually within 4 weeks of CSEC results being released. Late applications may not be considered for the September intake. ## How to apply It takes about 15 minutes to apply online. Start now ## What the form asks for 1. Your name, sex, date of birth, National ID number, home address, parish, mobile number and email address. 2. The school you attended for CSEC. 3. Your CSEC subjects and grades. 4. Your parent or guardian’s relationship to you, name, mobile number and email address. 5. Your Sixth Form school choices, in order of preference. 6. The CAPE subjects you would like to study. 7. Your supporting documents. 8. A declaration confirming the information you have given is true and correct. You can upload files in PDF, JPG, PNG or DOC format, up to 10 MB each. Each school offers its own subject combinations, known as ‘option blocks’. Your choices show the Ministry what you would like to study, but the school you are placed at may not offer that exact mix. ## After you apply You will get a reference number when you submit your application. 1. The Ministry reviews your application against each chosen school’s entry requirements. 2. Each school confirms which students it can take. 3. You will be told your placement by letter and email before the September intake. 4. Once you are placed, the school confirms which CAPE subjects are available.

pages.title: Apply for a special education bursary
pages.description: Apply for financial help towards your child’s fees at a private special-education provider in Barbados.
pages.body_markdown: If your child has additional learning needs that cannot be met in a government school, you can apply for a bursary towards their education at a private special-education provider in Barbados. The bursary covers part of the annual fees. It is means-tested and discretionary, and the exact amount is decided case by case by the Bursary Committee based on your child’s needs and your household circumstances. ## Who can apply You can apply if: - your child is a Barbadian citizen or legally resident in Barbados - your child has a documented diagnosis or assessed special education need - a government-school placement is not suitable for your child’s needs - a private special-education provider in Barbados has agreed to take your child If approved, the bursary covers one school year. You must reapply each year your child continues in the placement. ## Before you start It takes about 20 to 30 minutes once you have your documents. You’ll need to upload: 1. Your letter explaining the need for the bursary. 2. A medical or educational evaluation describing your child’s diagnosis or needs. 3. The provider’s acceptance letter confirming your child has been offered a place. You can also include proof of income for the past 3 months, but this is optional. ## How to apply You can apply online. Start now ## What the form asks for You’ll need to give: 1. Your child’s details — their name, date of birth, sex and National ID number. 2. Your child’s needs — their diagnosis or assessed needs, their current school or programme, and why a private provider is needed. 3. Your details as the parent or guardian — your name, National ID number, relationship to the child, home address, phone number and email address. 4. Your household circumstances — the number of people in your household, the number of dependent children, your employment status, your approximate monthly household income, and any other government support you receive for this child. 5. The private provider’s details — their name, address, phone number, the annual fees, the amount you are requesting and the expected start date. 6. Your bank or credit union account details. You’ll also need to confirm that your information is true and correct, that approval is discretionary and not guaranteed, and that you’ll report any changes in your child’s placement or your household circumstances. ## After you apply A bursary officer reviews your application and may call you for more information. Your application is then presented to the Bursary Committee. A decision can take up to 8 weeks. If approved, the bursary is normally paid directly to the provider on your behalf. In some cases it can instead be paid into your bank account. You’ll get a copy of your application by email. If you have not heard anything within 8 weeks, you can call +1 (246) 535-0760 or email specialed@mes.gov.bb.

pages.title: Apply for exemption from school attendance
pages.description: Apply for a Certificate of Exemption if your child cannot attend school in the usual way.
pages.body_markdown: If your child cannot attend school in the usual way — for example, because of a medical condition, a disability, religious reasons, or an extended family relocation — you can apply for a Certificate of Exemption under the Education Act. There is no fee. An exemption from attendance is not an exemption from education. Your child must continue to receive education during the exemption period. ## Who can apply You can apply if you are the parent or guardian of a child who cannot attend school in the usual way. You can apply for one of the following reasons: 1. A medical or health condition. 2. A disability that requires an alternative education arrangement. 3. A family relocation or extended travel. 4. A religious or cultural reason. 5. Home schooling — this needs a separate Home Schooling application. 6. Another reason, which you describe. An exemption is granted at the Ministry’s discretion and may be revoked if the conditions of the certificate are not met. ## Before you start You will need documents ready to upload: 1. The child’s birth certificate. 2. A medical report, if you are applying for a medical reason. 3. Any other supporting document. You can upload files in PDF, JPG, PNG or DOC format, up to 10 MB each. ## How to apply It takes about 15 minutes to apply online. Start now ## What the form asks for 1. Your title, name, National ID number, relationship to the child, home address, parish, mobile number and email address. 2. The child’s name, date of birth, sex and National ID or birth certificate number, along with their current school, last class and last date attended if they have attended school. 3. The reason you are applying and a description of your circumstances. 4. The start and end dates of the exemption you are requesting. 5. A description of how the child’s education will continue during the exemption. 6. Your supporting documents. 7. A declaration confirming the information you have given is true and correct. ## After you apply You will get a reference number when you submit your application. 1. An Education Officer reviews your application and may ask for more information. 2. The Chief Education Officer approves or declines the application. 3. You will be told the outcome within 6 weeks by letter and email. You must tell the Ministry promptly if your child’s circumstances change during the exemption period.

pages.title: Apply for secondary school entry for a non-national child
pages.description: Apply for a non-national child, or a child born outside Barbados, to attend a government secondary school.
pages.body_markdown: Use this service to apply for a non-national child — or a child born outside Barbados — to attend a government secondary school. There is no application fee. ## Who can apply You can apply for a child who is a non-national or who was born outside Barbados. If the child has refugee, asylum or stateless status, these cases need a different process — contact the Ministry directly. ## Before you start Gather your documents first. You will need: 1. The child’s birth certificate. 2. If you are a CARICOM national, your immigration status certificate. 3. If you are not a CARICOM national, the child’s immigration status certificate. You can upload files in PDF, JPG or PNG format, up to 10 MB each. You can also choose to submit physical copies in person. ## How to apply It takes about 10 minutes to apply online. Start now ## What the form asks for 1. The child’s first name, surname and any other names. 2. The child’s country of birth, sex and date of birth. 3. The name of the school the child currently attends. 4. The preferred secondary school in Barbados. 5. Your title, name, address in Barbados, contact number, email address and country of birth. 6. Your immigration status in Barbados. 7. Documents to upload. 8. A declaration confirming the information you have given is true and correct. ## After you apply You will get a reference number when you submit your application. 1. The Ministry will review your application and the documents. 2. You will be contacted by the school within 4 weeks. 3. A confirmation email will be sent to the address you gave. If you chose to submit physical copies of your documents, take them to the school as soon as possible to avoid delays.

pages.title: Apply for term’s leave
pages.description: Teachers at public schools in Barbados can apply for extended leave during a school term.
pages.body_markdown: If you are a teacher at a public school in Barbados, you can use this form to apply for term’s leave. This is extended leave taken during a school term, and is separate from maternity, sick or sabbatical leave. ## Who can apply This form is for teachers at public schools in Barbados. Your leave: - cannot be more than 1 year long - cannot start more than 30 days in the past - cannot start more than 18 months in the future The length of your leave is calculated from normal teaching days only. Public holidays and school breaks within the period do not extend it. ## How to apply You can apply online. It takes about 10 minutes once you have your information ready. Start now ## What the form asks for - your details — your school, name, National ID number and your post or job title - your contact number and email address - your leave dates — your start and end dates, and whether you have previously been granted term’s leave - a brief explanation of why you are requesting leave. Your reason is confidential and we share it only with your principal and our HR team You’ll also need to confirm that your information is true and correct, and that you understand your principal and the Ministry will review the application. ## After you apply When you submit your application, you will get a copy by email along with a unique reference number. Your principal will review it and forwards it to the Ministry with a recommendation to approve or decline. The Ministry makes the final decision and contacts you with the outcome within 15 working days of receiving your application. If you need help, you can call the Ministry of Educational Transformation at 535-0600.

pages.title: Apply for National Summer Camp Science Programme 2026
pages.description: Apply for a child to attend Tropical Trails and Tales Science Camp 2026 (13 July to 21 August 2026).
pages.body_markdown: Use this service to apply for a child to attend Tropical Trails and Tales Science Camp 2026. This camp is part of the National Summer Camp Programme. There is no fee to apply or attend camp. Applying does not mean the child has a place. ## Who can apply You can apply if you are the child's parent or guardian. The child must be 12 to 15 years old. ## Before you start Have these details ready: - the child's date of birth - your email address and phone number - a phone number for another adult we can contact in an emergency - details of any health condition, allergy, medicine or food need - the name and phone number for the child's doctor or polyclinic, if they have one - names and phone numbers for people allowed to collect the child, if the child cannot make their own way home ## About the camp The camp runs from 13 July to 21 August 2026, Monday to Friday, 9am to 3pm. Camp activities take place at: - Welchman Hall Seventh-day Adventist Church, Vault Road, Welchman Hall, St. Thomas - Natural Heritage Department Grounds, #1 Sturges, St. Thomas ## When you can apply Applications close on 5 July 2026. The Ministry will contact you by 7 July 2026 if the child gets a place. ## What happens after you apply The Ministry will review your application and contact you about the next steps. ## If you need help For help with Tropical Trails and Tales Science Camp 2026, contact: Telephone: (246) 535-3846 or (246) 832-2507 Email: [doyaresearchunit@gmail.com](mailto:doyaresearchunit@gmail.com) Start now

pages.title: Apply to home-school your child
pages.description: Apply for permission to home-school your child in Barbados.
pages.body_markdown: Use this service to apply for permission to home-school your child in Barbados. Permission must be granted by the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Educational Transformation. There is no application fee. ## Who can apply You can apply if you are the parent or guardian of a child you want to home-school. ## Before you start You will need to: - follow the National Curriculum or an alternative approved curriculum. - attend an in-person interview before permission can be granted. - provide regular progress reports for each child. You will also need documents ready to upload, including a timetable that covers English, Mathematics, Science, Social Studies and Physical Activity, and certification for each tutor. ## How to apply It takes about 20 minutes to apply online. Start now ## What the form asks for - your name, address, phone number, email address and residency status in Barbados. - how many children you want to home-school, and each child’s full name and date of birth. - whether any of the children attended school before, and if so the school’s name and address. - how many tutors will teach the children, and each tutor’s name and qualifications. - your reasons for home-schooling, including your plans for socialisation, sports and learning outside the home. - documents to upload — a timetable and tutor certification. You can also upload an alternative curriculum and previous progress reports if you have them. - a declaration confirming the information you have given is true and correct. You can upload files in PDF, JPG, PNG or DOC format, up to 10 MB each. ## After you apply You will get a reference number when you submit your application. Our Nursery and Primary Section will review your application and call you to arrange an interview within 3 weeks. The interview helps the Ministry decide whether to grant permission. The Permanent Secretary grants or refuses written permission after the interview. A copy will be emailed to you once your application has been processed.

pages.title: Apply to sit the BSSEE early
pages.description: Apply for your child to sit the BSSEE ahead of their year group if they are academically ready.
pages.body_markdown: If your child is academically ready to take the Barbados Secondary Schools’ Entrance Examination (BSSEE) ahead of their year group, for example at age 10 instead of 11, you can apply for them to sit it early. Your child will be given only one opportunity to write the examination. If they sit early and do not do well, they cannot re-sit the BSSEE. ## Who can apply You can apply if you are the parent or legal guardian of a primary school child and: - your child is at least 9 years old on 31 August - your child is currently enrolled in primary school, from Infants A through to Class 4 - your child’s school Principal supports the application ## Before you start Apply before the BSSEE registration deadline, usually in late January. Decisions are made by the Ministry and are at its discretion. ## How to apply You can complete the online form. It takes about 10 minutes. Start now ## What the form asks for 1. Your details as the parent or guardian, including your title, name, National ID number, home address, mobile number, email address and your relationship to the child. 2. Your child’s name and date of birth. 3. Which BSSEE sitting year you are applying for. 4. Your child’s current school and class. 5. Why your child is ready to sit early, and a summary of your supporting evidence. You must upload the Principal’s recommendation letter. You can also upload test scores or school reports and any other supporting document. You confirm that the information is true, that you understand your child has only one examination attempt, that the Principal supports the request, and that the decision rests with the Ministry. ## After you apply You will get a copy of your application at the email address you provide. The Ministry reviews your request and may consult your child’s primary school. You will be told the outcome by letter and phone within 4 weeks. If approved, your child is registered for that year’s BSSEE.

pages.title: Choose secondary schools for the BSSEE
pages.description: Rank the secondary schools you would like your child to attend after they sit the BSSEE.
pages.body_markdown: ## Who can use this service You can use this service if you are the parent or guardian of a child sitting the BSSEE. Use it to rank the secondary schools you would like your child to attend. ## How to choose your schools You can complete the form online. It takes about 15 minutes. Start now ## What the form asks for - your child’s name, current address, date of birth, sex, National ID number, current primary school and country of birth - your details as the parent or guardian, including your title, name, National ID number, phone number and email address. - your child’s assigned zone - 9 school choices: 2 from any school and 7 from your assigned zone - whether you are willing to consider a private school placement. - a declaration confirming that the information provided is accurate, that you are submitting only one form, and that you understand how placement works ## After you submit your choices Once your form has been processed, you will receive a reference number and a confirmation email will be sent to the email address you provided. You will be told your child’s school placement within 4 to 6 weeks of the results being released. If you need help, contact the Ministry of Educational Transformation at 535-0600.

pages.title: Claim examination travel expenses
pages.description: Claim reimbursement for travel you made on official examination business as a teacher or exam-centre staff member.
pages.body_markdown: If you are a teacher or a member of exam-centre staff, you can claim reimbursement for travel you made on official examination business. This includes travel for invigilation, marking sessions, exam centre setup, and collecting or returning papers. ## Who can claim If you are a teacher or examination centre staff member, you can claim payment for travel costs made on official examination business. This includes travel for invigilation, marking sessions, examination centre setup, and collecting or returning papers. ## Before you start There is no fee to make a claim. You must submit one claim per month, and each form must cover one month of travel. You do not need receipts for mileage claims, but you must use the published Civil Service mileage rate. For other expenses, you must upload your receipts. ## How to claim You can claim online. The form takes about 10 to 15 minutes, depending on how many trips you are claiming for. Start now ## What the form asks for - your personal details (surname, first names, National ID number, school or examination centre, home address, mobile number and email address) - travel period (the month and year you are claiming for) - trip details (number of trips, and for each trip the date, where you travelled from and to, the purpose, and the amount claimed in Barbados dollars) - receipts (supporting receipts where required for non-mileage expenses) - declaration (confirmation that the trips were made on official examination business, that the information provided is correct, and that you understand the penalty for false information) ## After you claim Your claim will be reviewed and approved by the Examinations Officer, Deputy Permanent Secretary and Accounts Officer. You can expect payment through your school payroll within 6 weeks. A confirmation email will be sent to the email address you provided. If you need help, contact the Ministry of Educational Transformation at 535-0600.

pages.title: Claim payment for examination duties
pages.description: Claim payment for duties you performed during an examination period, such as invigilation, supervision or assessment.
pages.body_markdown: ## Who can claim If you performed duties during a recent examination period, you can claim payment for your work. Use this service if you worked as an: - invigilator - supervisor - examination assessor - door marshal - centre clerk - reader - writer - interpreter - model - moderator - dictator You can also use this service if you helped with practical examination setup. ## Before you start There is no fee to make a claim. All amounts are in Barbados dollars. You will need: - the examination period and the dates your duties covered - the details of each duty, including the centre, your role and the rate - your bank or credit union account details for payment ## How to claim You can apply online. It takes about 15 to 45 minutes, depending on how many duties you are claiming for. Start now ## What the form asks for - your personal details (name, National ID number, contact details and supervisor’s name) - exam period and date range covered - details of duties (date, centre, role, rate, and any relevant subject or candidates) - payment details (bank or credit union, branch, account number and type, and name on the account) - a declaration confirming the information is correct ## After you claim Once your supervisor approves your claim, payment will be made directly to your account within 4 to 6 weeks after the examination period ends. You will get an email when the payment has been processed. If your claim has not been paid after 6 weeks, contact the Examinations Section at 535-0600.

pages.title: Defer your child’s BSSEE sitting
pages.description: Ask the Ministry for a one-year deferral if your child is not yet ready to sit the BSSEE.
pages.body_markdown: If your 11-year-old child is not yet ready to sit the Barbados Secondary Schools’ Entrance Examination (BSSEE), use this form to request a one-year deferral. A deferral means your child sits the exam the following year. Your child will be given only one opportunity to write the examination. ## Who can apply You can apply if you are the parent or guardian of a child who is around 10 to 12 years old on 31 August. ## Before you start Submit your request before the BSSEE registration window closes, usually in late January. Approval is at the Ministry’s discretion. ## How to apply You can complete the online form. Start now ## What the form asks for 1. Your child’s current primary school, name and date of birth. 2. Your details as the parent or guardian, including your title, name, address, contact number and email address. 3. Your reason for the deferral, such as low academic performance in Mathematics or English, missed instruction due to trauma or illness, or significant learning difficulties. 4. A written explanation of why your child is not ready. You can also upload supporting documents, such as a medical letter or a school report or assessment. Each file can be a PDF, JPG, PNG or DOC and up to 10 MB. You confirm that the information is true and correct, that you understand your child has only one opportunity to write the examination, and that approval is at the Ministry’s discretion. ## After you apply You will get a confirmation email at the address you provide. The Ministry will review your request, consult your child’s primary school where needed, and respond within 4 weeks. The decision is communicated by letter and phone. If your request is approved, your child is automatically registered for next year’s exam. If it is denied, your child sits the exam as originally scheduled.

pages.title: Refer a student for support
pages.description: School staff can refer a student to the Student Support Services Unit for additional help.
pages.body_markdown: If you are a member of school staff, you can use this form to refer a student to the Student Support Services Unit (SSSU). The unit helps students who are facing difficulties in school. ## Who can refer a student This form is for school staff, such as teachers, counsellors and administrators, referring a student on behalf of their school. Before you submit a referral, you should have: - consulted the student’s parent or guardian and discussed the difficulties with them within the last 18 months - completed a Student Profile Form after a period of classroom observation - got approval from your principal ## How to refer You can complete the referral online. It takes about 15 minutes. Start now ## What the form asks for You’ll need to give: - the student’s details — their name, National ID number, date of birth, sex and home address - the parent or guardian details — names, relationships and contact numbers, and who the student lives with most of the time - the school details — the school name, the student’s class or form, and the school telephone number - a description of the student’s challenges, and the difficulties you have observed - the student’s attendance pattern and any outside agencies already involved - what the school has tried so far - your details as the referrer — your name, role, email address and the date you consulted the parent or guardian You can also upload supporting documents: - student Profile Form - clinical or psychological reports - school or attendance records You'll need to confirm that: - the parent or guardian has been consulted - your information is true and correct - the principal has approved the referral ## After you submit a referral We will assign a caseworker, who will contact the school within 3 weeks. The caseworker will meet the student and consult the parent or guardian. If we need more information before assigning a caseworker, we will email or phone you. You will get a reference number for future correspondence. If you have additional reports later, you can email them to studentsupportservices@mes.gov.bb with your reference number.

pages.title: Register as a private CAPE candidate
pages.description: Register online to sit the Caribbean Advanced Proficiency Examination (CAPE) as a private candidate.
pages.body_markdown: ## Who can register If you are not registered for the Caribbean Advanced Proficiency Examination (CAPE) through a school, you can register as a private candidate. You can use this service to choose the subjects you want to take. ## Before you start CXC sets registration deadlines, and late registration is not accepted. Check the CXC website for this year’s deadline before you start. CXC charges a fee for each subject. You will be told the total fees due after you submit your registration. ## How to register You can apply online. It takes about 10 to 20 minutes to complete, depending on the number of subjects you are entering. Start now ## What the form asks for - your name, date of birth, sex and National ID number - your home address, telephone number and email address - the number of subjects you are registering for For each subject: - subject name - unit (unit 1 or unit 2) - whether you are taking an alternative paper - whether it is a resit - previous registration number (if it is a resit) - a declaration confirming that your information is accurate, that you have checked for timetable clashes, and that you will notify the registrar if your name changes ## After you register The CXC Local Registrar will check your registration and confirm your candidate number and the fees due. You will then receive instructions on how to pay. Your timetable and examination centre details are sent closer to the examination date, and a confirmation email is sent to the email address you provided. If you need help, contact the CXC Local Registrar at 535-0600 or by email at examssection@mes.gov.bb

pages.title: Register as a private CSEC candidate
pages.description: Register online to sit the Caribbean Secondary Education Certificate (CSEC) as a private candidate.
pages.body_markdown: ## Who can register You can register as a private candidate if you are not registered for CSEC through a school. You can choose when to take the exam and the subjects you want to take. ## Before you start Registration deadlines are set by CXC, and late registration is not accepted. Check the CXC website for this year’s deadline before you start. CXC charges a fee for each subject. You will be told the fees due after you submit your registration. ## How to register You can apply online. It takes about 10 to 20 minutes to complete, depending on the number of subjects you are entering. Start now ## What the form asks for - your name, date of birth, sex and National ID number - your home address, telephone number and email address - which sitting you prefer (January or May/June) - how many subjects you want to enter - the subject name, whether you are taking an alternative paper, and whether it is a resit. If it is a resit, you must also give your previous registration number - a declaration confirming your information is accurate, that you have checked for any timetable clashes, and that you’ll tell the registrar if your name changes ## After you register The CXC Local Registrar will check your registration and confirm your candidate number and the fees due. You will then receive instructions on how to pay. Your timetable and examination centre details are sent closer to the examination date. A confirmation email is also sent to the email address you provided. If you need help, contact the CXC Local Registrar at 535-0600 or by email at examssection@mes.gov.bb

pages.title: Request a BSSEE school reallocation
pages.description: Ask the Ministry to change the secondary school your child was allocated after the BSSEE results.
pages.body_markdown: If your child has been allocated to a secondary school you would like to change after the BSSEE results have been published, you can ask the Ministry to reallocate them. Reallocation depends on space being available and is not guaranteed. ## Who can apply You can apply if you are the parent or guardian of a child who received a BSSEE allocation and you want to request a different school. ## Before you start Submit your request within the window the Ministry announces after the BSSEE results, usually 2 to 3 weeks. Late requests will not be considered for the September intake. ## How to apply You can complete the online form. Start now ## What the form asks for 1. Your details as the parent or guardian, including your title, name, National ID number, relationship to the child, home address, parish, mobile number and email address. 2. Your child’s name, date of birth, sex and primary school attended. 3. Your child’s BSSEE composite score and candidate number. 4. Your child’s current school allocation. 5. Your first-choice school for reallocation, and a second choice if you have one. 6. Your reason for the reallocation. You must upload your child’s BSSEE results slip and birth certificate. You can also add notes and any other supporting document. You confirm that the information is accurate, that you understand reallocation is not guaranteed, and that you accept the original allocation if your request is declined. ## After you apply You will get a reference number straight away. You will be told the outcome by letter and email before the September intake. If your request is approved, the new allocation replaces the original. If it is declined, the original allocation stands.

pages.title: Request a statement of examination results
pages.description: Request an official statement of your past examination results from the Ministry of Educational Transformation.
pages.body_markdown: You can request an official statement of your past examination results from the Ministry of Educational Transformation. This covers exams such as CSEC, CAPE, BSSEE, City and Guilds, Cambridge and GCE. ## Who can apply This service is for anyone who needs an official statement of results for exams they sat through the Ministry. You can also apply on behalf of someone else if you have their authorisation. ## Before you start You must pay the processing fee before you submit the form. Pay at the Ministry’s Accounts Department, then upload the receipt as proof. Statements are not issued until the fee is paid and the receipt is verified. You’ll need to upload: 1. A government-issued photo ID. 2. Your receipt of payment. 3. An authorisation letter, if you are applying on behalf of someone else. The form takes about 10 minutes to complete. ## How to apply Start now ## What the form asks for 1. Your title, surname as it appeared on your exam entry, first names and any maiden or former name. 2. Your National ID number, date of birth, home address, mobile number and email address. 3. The examination body, the series or sitting, your candidate number if you have it, and the school or centre where you sat the exam. 4. The subjects you want on the statement and your reason for needing it. 5. How you’d like to receive the statement: collect in person at the Examinations Unit, by post, or by courier. If you choose post or courier, you’ll give a delivery address. ## After you apply The Examinations Unit verifies your identity and payment, locates your records and prepares your statement. Statements are normally ready within 10 working days and sent by the method you chose. A confirmation email is sent to the address you gave. If you need help, you can contact the Examinations Unit by phone on (246) 535-0600 or by email at exams@mes.gov.bb.

pages.title: Request special arrangements for the BSSEE
pages.description: Ask for access arrangements, such as extra time or a separate room, so your child can sit the BSSEE on equal terms.
pages.body_markdown: If your child needs special arrangements to sit the Barbados Secondary Schools’ Entrance Examination (BSSEE) on equal terms, you can request access arrangements. Examples include extra time, a separate room, large-print papers, a reader or a medical adjustment. There is no fee. ## Who can apply You can apply if you are the parent or guardian of a child taking the BSSEE. ## Before you start Submit your request at least 6 weeks before the BSSEE so the Ministry has time to set up the arrangement. The decision is at the Ministry’s discretion. ## How to apply You can complete the online form. It takes about 10 minutes. Start now ## What the form asks for 1. Your details as the parent or guardian, including your title, name, National ID number, home address, mobile number and email address. 2. Your child’s name and date of birth. 3. Which BSSEE sitting year you are applying for. 4. Your child’s current school and class. 5. The type of arrangement needed, such as medical, learning, physical or other. 6. A description of the arrangement needed and the supporting reason. Depending on the type of request, you may need to upload a medical, specialist or psychologist report. You can also upload the Principal’s letter and any other supporting document. You confirm that the information is true and correct, that your child’s Principal is aware of the request, that the Ministry may share information with exam centre staff, and that the decision is at the Ministry’s discretion. ## After you apply You will get a reference number, and a copy is sent to your email address. The Ministry will review your request, consult your child’s primary school Principal, and respond within 3 weeks by letter and phone. If approved, the arrangement is communicated to the exam centre before exam day.

pages.title: Apply for a place at a day nursery
pages.description: Apply for a place at a government-run day nursery in Barbados for young children. Nurseries provide early childhood education and care.
pages.body_markdown:
Parents and guardians of children under the age of 5 can apply for them to go to a government-run day nursery. Nursery places are decided on a case-by-case basis. It is a good idea to apply for at least 3 nurseries.

## When to apply

You can apply for a place as soon as a child is born. However, if your application is successful, the child cannot start attending the nursery until they are 3 months old.

Applications are open all year round.

## How to apply

### Get an application form

This service is not available online yet so you must go to each nursery you want to apply to. (Three is recommended). A supervisor completes an application form for you, and will ask:

- your name

- your address

- your contact number

- the child’s name

- the child’s date of birth

- the child’s sex

- if the child has allergies and/or medical conditions

- your relationship to the child

### What to take

You will need to take your child’s Green Book which has their medical background recorded.

### Before you leave the nursery

The supervisor will give you a copy of the completed form. You should refer to the application number on the form if you need to contact the nursery again.

## After you’ve applied

The supervisor and a senior officer for the daycare programme will check your eligibility and whether there’s space for your child in the nursery you’ve applied to.

### If your application is successful

If your child is eligible and a place is available, they will be enrolled at the nursery immediately, or, at the start of the new term in September.

Before your child begins daycare, you will be invited to an orientation session so you can get to know the nursery, sign the acceptance document, and recap on your child’s allergies and medical conditions

### What to bring to the orientation

You will need to share:

1. A photocopy of the child’s birth certificate to confirm their mother’s, father’s name if included and the child’s date of birth.

2. Passport-sized photo of child for identification and their file

### If your application is unsuccessful

If your child is eligible but a place is not currently available, they will be put on a reserve list.

## Accessibility

If you cannot attend the nursery to complete an application form, you can send a representative. However, a parent or guardian must attend the orientation session.

pages.title: Get a copy of a birth certificate
pages.description: Apply online to get a certified copy of a birth certificate for anyone whose birth was registered in Barbados. Certificates are issued by the Registration Department.
pages.body_markdown:
This service can be used to get a copy of a birth certificate for anyone whose birth was registered in Barbados. Most copies of birth certificates are requested at the same time a birth is registered as part of the [Register a birth service](/family-birth-relationships/register-a-birth). A copy is essential for access to certain public services and welfare support. However, copies for Barbadian citizens can be requested at any point. They are needed as official identification so you can apply for a passport or driving licence, and as proof of identity in financial or legal-related matters such as opening a bank account or getting married. You can request a copy on someone else’s behalf but you must disclose: - your relationship to them - why you need the certificate ## How to get a copy of a birth certificate ### Complete the form There are 2 ways to get a copy of a birth certificate. You can: 1. #### Request a copy online You must pay online so you will need a debit or credit card, and you will need to have (or create) an EZPay+ account.
Every question is compulsory so if you are unsure about the basic information asked for, you should complete the paper form instead. Complete the online form 2. #### Get a paper Application for birth certificate form from the Registration Department You must complete it by hand and return it to the department. You can pay with cash or by card when you collect it.
If you are unsure about the basic details asked for (for example, if there is estrangement in the family), you should complete the paper form. Registration Department
Supreme Court Complex
Whitepark Road
St. Michael
(246) 535-9700
Open Monday to Friday: 8:30am to 3:15pm ## Cost of certificates Each certified copy costs $5 BBD. People aged 60 and over pay $1 BBD per certificate. ## After your request is processed A certificate is usually ready to collect in 5 to 7 business days. A certificate can sometimes be issued on the same day, in the case of a medical or travel emergency. You will need to show proof of the emergency. If you complete the paper form, you will be given a receipt when you return it to the Applications Desk at the Registration Department. You will need to show your receipt when you collect your copy or copies and you will be able to pay in cash or by card. ## If basic information is unknown There are circumstances when you may not be able to provide all the information asked for in the form. For example, if there is estrangement in the family, or if the birth was registered in Barbados a significant time ago. In these cases you must complete a paper form and provide as much information as you can – the more details you can give, the better the chance of finding the records you are looking for. ## Get a copy of a birth certificate if you live overseas Contact the Registration Department. [registrarsupremecourt@barbados.gov.bb](mailto:registrarsupremecourt@barbados.gov.bb) (246) 535-9700 +1 (246) 535-9751 (if you are calling from overseas)

pages.title: Register a birth
pages.description: Register a birth in Barbados online. All births must be legally registered within 28 days. A birth registration is required before a birth certificate can be issued.
pages.body_markdown:
It is a legal requirement that all births in Barbados (including stillbirths) are registered within 28 days. However, there is a grace period of 1 year. After this point, you will pay a late registration fee.

Before a birth certificate can be issued, the birth must be registered. The certificate is essential for access to public services including school enrollment and certain health services.

---

## How to register a birth

1. Take your documents (listed below) to the registry office in the district where the child was born. You cannot book an appointment but lunchtime is typically busy.

2. A registration clerk will use your documents to verify your identity. They will then record the baby’s full name, date and place of birth, parents’ details, for example, their name, occupations and address.

3. When you have reviewed and confirmed the details, the registration clerk will ask you to sign the official register.

4. The clerk will begin the process of issuing a birth certificate which will be ready to collect in 2 to 3 days. Each certified copy costs BDS $5.00.

---

## Who should register a birth?

You cannot register a birth online yet, so you need to do it in person in the district where the child was born.

If the parents are:

- married to each other, the father must register and the mother can attend

- not married to each other, the mother must register the birth but it is not necessary for the father to attend

- not married to each other but the father wants to be named on the birth record, both parents must register the birth together

You do not need to take the baby.

---

## What to bring

You need to show:

1. Your child’s Personal Child Health Record from the hospital or birthing centre (sometimes called the immunisation book or birth notification).

2. A valid form of photo identification for each parent who will be named on the birth record.  
   For Barbadian citizens, your Barbados National ID card, valid passport or other government-issued ID is acceptable. Non-Barbadian nationals must show their valid passport.

3. Your original marriage certificate if you are married to the child’s other parent.

#### Parents who are minors

If you are a mother or a father and you are under 16 years old, you are considered a minor.

If you have a valid passport, you must bring:

- your valid passport

- your original birth certificate

- the child’s medical book (green book)

You must be accompanied by your parent(s) or guardian(s).

If you do not have a valid passport, you must bring:

- your minor’s identification card

- your original birth certificate

- the child’s medical book (green book)

- an identification letter signed by a Justice of the Peace

You must be accompanied by your parent(s) or guardian(s).

If you don’t meet these criteria, contact the Registrations Department.

---

## If you are unable to register the birth in person

If you are unable to attend in person, contact the Registration Department in Bridgetown as soon as possible after the child is born.

Registration Department  
Supreme Court Complex  
Whitepark Road  
St. Michael  
(246) 535-9700

---

## Late registrations

Births must be registered within 28 days of the child being born. There is a grace period of 1 year but after this point, the parent or guardian must engage a legal assistant from the Registrations Department to help with the late registration process. You will need to pay a late registration fee of BDS $20.00.

---

## Where to register

You cannot register a birth online yet, so you need to do it in person in the district where the child was born. Even if this is not the closest magistrate’s court to where you live.

#### Born in St. Michael (District A)

Go to the Registration Department (Records Branch), in the Supreme Court Complex, Whitepark Road, St. Michael

#### Born in Christ Church or St. George

Go to the District B Magistrate’s Court, currently located at the Eric Holder Municipal Complex, Blackmans, St. Joseph

#### Born in St. Philip or St. John

Normally located at the District C Magistrate’s Court, St. Matthias, Christ Church, currently located at the Registration Department, in the Supreme Court Complex, Whitepark Road, St. Michael

#### Born in St. Thomas

Go to the District D Magistrate’s Court, Cane Carden St. Thomas

#### Born in St. Peter, St. James, or St. Lucy

Go to the District E Magistrate’s Court, Holetown, St. James

#### Born in St. Joseph or St. Andrew

Go to the District F Magistrate’s Court, Eric Holder Municipal Complex, Blackmans, St. Joseph

If you are unsure of your district please contact the Registration Department at the Supreme Court.

pages.title: Find a pharmacy and check what Barbados Drug Service benefits it offers
pages.description: Find a pharmacy that's open now anywhere in Barbados. You can also find pharmacies offering free or subsidised medication through the Barbados Drug Service, and check who qualifies.
pages.body_markdown: If you are eligible, you can get prescription medication free at a government polyclinic pharmacy or pay a small dispensing fee at a private pharmacy that participates in the government subsidy programme. This service is provided through the Special Benefit Service (SBS). The Barbados Drug Service (BDS) pays the pharmacy on your behalf. Find an open pharmacy ## What to take to the pharmacy - your prescription - original accepted ID for the person the medication is for: a Barbados National Identification (ID) card, passport or child health book. A child health book is only accepted for children up to 6 weeks old. After 6 weeks, an ID card is required. Photocopies are not accepted. ## Collecting for someone else Medication must be collected in person. This service is not available online. Someone else can collect for you. They will need to bring your prescription, your ID, and their own ID. ## Get free or subsidised medication Some pharmacies can lower or remove the cost of your prescription medication through the Barbados Drug Service if you qualify. Medication is free at government (polyclinic) pharmacies and costs less at private pharmacies that work with the Drug Service. Not all private pharmacies take part. At those pharmacies, you pay full price. [Check who qualifies and what to bring](/health-and-emergency-services/free-or-subsidised-medication) ## Prescription colours Prescriptions in Barbados come in different colours. The colour of your prescription can affect which pharmacy can fill it. [Check what the prescription colours mean](/health-and-emergency-services/prescription-colours) ## Get help If a pharmacy will not accept your Drug Service prescription, or you have a problem getting your medication, contact the Drug Service. Telephone: [(246) 535-4300](tel:+12465354300) Email: [management@drugservice.gov.bb](mailto:management@drugservice.gov.bb) Website: [drugservice.gov.bb](https://drugservice.gov.bb) Address: 6th Floor, Warrens Tower II

pages.title: Get free or subsidised medication
pages.description: Check who can get free or cheaper medication through the Barbados Drug Service, what to bring to the pharmacy, and what it costs.
pages.body_markdown: The Barbados Drug Service can make some prescription medications free or cheaper through the government subsidy (officially the Special Benefit Service). This page explains who can get help, what to bring, and what it costs. - free at government (polyclinic) pharmacies - at a lower cost at private pharmacies that work with the Drug Service ## Who can get help with medication costs You can get help if you are a Barbadian citizen or permanent resident. One of these must also apply: - you need medication for diabetes, asthma, high blood pressure, cancer, epilepsy or glaucoma (any age) - you are under 16 - you are 65 or over You will also need: - a prescription from a doctor registered with the Medical Council of Barbados. The doctor can work in the public or private health service - a prescription for a medication on the Barbados National Drug Formulary Not all medication is free, even where a patient is eligible for benefits. Some medicines or repeat items may still have a cost, including certain antihistamines. If you are travelling, you can only get up to two months' supply of medication. You will need to pay for any medication not covered by the Special Benefit Service (SBS). The Barbados National Drug Formulary is the list of medications covered by the Drug Service. [Check if your medication is listed](https://formulary.drugservice.gov.bb/bndf2022/menu.php) **What if my medication is not listed?** Ask your doctor: - if there is another listed medication you can use - if they can ask for special approval Special approval is only for government pharmacy use. ## What to take to the pharmacy - your prescription - original accepted ID for the person the medication is for: a Barbados National Identification (ID) card, passport or child health book. A child health book is only accepted for children up to 6 weeks old. After 6 weeks, an ID card is required. Photocopies are not accepted. Find an open pharmacy ## What you may pay - At a government pharmacy, there is no fee to prepare your medication. - At a private pharmacy that works with the Drug Service, you pay a fee to prepare your medication. This is called a dispensing fee. The amount depends on the medication. - At a private pharmacy that is not part of the Drug Service, you pay the full price. ## Prescription colour The colour of your prescription can affect which pharmacies can fill it. [Check what the prescription colours mean](/health-and-emergency-services/prescription-colours) ## Need help at the pharmacy? You may need help if: - your ID is not accepted - the pharmacy asks you to pay more than expected - the pharmacy is out of stock Contact the Drug Service. Telephone: [(246) 535-4300](tel:+12465354300) Email: [management@drugservice.gov.bb](mailto:management@drugservice.gov.bb) Website: [drugservice.gov.bb](https://drugservice.gov.bb) Address: 6th Floor, Warrens Tower II

pages.title: What prescription colours mean
pages.description: What the different prescription colours mean in Barbados, and how the colour can affect which pharmacy can fill your prescription.
pages.body_markdown:
Prescriptions in Barbados come in different colours. The colour of your prescription can affect which pharmacy can fill it. Where you can use your prescription also depends on where it came from.

## Blue prescription

This is usually from a public polyclinic or outpatient clinic.

You can take it to:

-   a government pharmacy
-   a participating private pharmacy

At a participating private pharmacy, you pay a fee to prepare your medication. This is called a dispensing fee.

## Yellow or green prescription

This is usually from the Queen Elizabeth Hospital.

You can take it to:

-   the Queen Elizabeth Hospital pharmacy
-   some government pharmacies, for selected medications

If you take it to a participating private pharmacy, you may have to pay the full cost.

## Pink prescription

This is usually from a private doctor.

You can take it to:

-   a government pharmacy
-   a participating private pharmacy

At a participating private pharmacy, you pay a fee to prepare your medication. This is called a dispensing fee. Some medications may still cost money.

## White prescription

White prescriptions can only be taken to a private pharmacy.

## If you are not sure

Ask the pharmacist to check before you pay. You can also contact the Barbados Drug Service.

Telephone: [(246) 535-4300](tel:+12465354300)

Email: [management@drugservice.gov.bb](mailto:management@drugservice.gov.bb)

Website: [drugservice.gov.bb](https://drugservice.gov.bb)

Address: 6th Floor, Warrens Tower II

pages.title: StormReady Barbados
pages.description: Get ready for hurricane season with a household preparation checklist and key contacts, and stay up to date with Department of Emergency Management (DEM) alerts.
pages.body_markdown: Hurricane season runs from 1 June to 30 November 2026. Prepare before the season starts — do not wait for a storm warning. ## Household checklist Use this checklist to make sure your household is ready for a hurricane. It covers water, food, documents, first aid, communication, and the steps to take before a storm. Open household checklist Save checklist as PDF The checklist lets you tick items off and saves your progress on this device. “Save checklist as PDF” opens the checklist and prompts your browser to save or print a copy. ### Highlights from the checklist Store at least 3 gallons of drinking water per person for 3 days. Fill baths, buckets and other containers before a storm. Keep your national ID, insurance documents and birth certificates in a waterproof bag. Have cash in small bills available. Charge all devices and power banks. Keep a battery-powered radio to receive DEM updates. Write down important phone numbers and emergency contacts. Board up windows if needed, bring in outdoor items, fill your vehicle with gas, and make sure family members know your emergency plan and shelter arrangements. ## Key contacts during a storm Tap a number to call. Lines can be busy during a storm — keep trying.

pages.title: Apply for an NHC rental unit or lot
pages.description: Use this service to apply to rent a unit or a lot from the National Housing Corporation (NHC). You must have a monthly income of BDS $3,000 or less to apply.
pages.body_markdown: Use this service to apply to rent a unit or a lot from the National Housing Corporation (NHC). ## Who can apply You can apply if you are: - a Barbadian citizen or permanent resident - earning a monthly income of BDS $3,000 or less If your monthly income is more than BDS $3,000, you will not be able to continue with the application. ## Before you start You will need: - your National Identification (ID) Number, which is on your national ID card - your TAMIS number, if you have one - two recent pay slips - your national ID card - a job letter from your employer - a passport-size photograph - co-applicant details, if you are applying jointly - details of all the people who will live in the unit ## Complete the form Allow about 20 minutes to complete the form. You should complete your application in one go. At the moment, it is not possible to save your answers and come back to them later. Start now ## Cost There is no cost to apply for an NHC rental unit or lot. ## What happens after you apply You will get a reference number and a confirmation email. Keep the reference number in case you need to contact NHC about your application. NHC will review your application and contact you within 10 working days. Submitting an application does not mean that you have been offered a rental unit or lot. ## Contact If you need help with your application, contact the National Housing Corporation.

pages.title: Application to Purchase Land or Property
pages.description: The National Housing Corporation (NHC) sells land and homes to people who do not already own land or property. Use this service to apply to buy an NHC lot or house.
pages.body_markdown: The National Housing Corporation (NHC) sells land and homes to people who do not already own land or property. Use this service to apply to buy an NHC lot or house. ## Who can apply You can apply if you **do not already own land or property**. People who already own land or a home are not eligible. You can apply on your own, or with a co-applicant, such as a partner or family member who will live in the home with you. ## What you can apply for You can apply to buy: - a 2-bedroom or 3-bedroom NHC home - a lot to build on (low-income lots are usually 3,000 to 4,000 square feet) Homes are built in timber, wall, timber-and-wall, or steel frame. You can say which type you prefer. NHC may offer you a property in a different parish from the one you ask for, depending on what is available. ## What you need before you start You will need: - your National Identification (ID) number - your TAMIS number - contact details we can reach you on - details of your employer, salary, and pay period - the number of adults and children in your household, and the children's ages - details of anyone in the household who has a disability - details of any other income in your household, such as maintenance, alimony, or a second job You will also need **one of the following**, depending on how you are paying: - a **bank statement**, if you are paying in cash - a **mortgage certificate**, if you are using a mortgage or loan If you already have land and want NHC to build on it, and you are a tenant of that land, you will also need a **letter of permission from your landlord**. ## Cost There is no application fee to apply to the National Housing Corporation (NHC) for the purchase of land or property. The price of the home or lot depends on the development. NHC will tell you the price when they make you an offer. ## How long does it take? Completing an application form typically takes 15 to 20 minutes. The length of time it takes to receive an offer from the NHC varies and depends on several factors, including eligibility, the availability of land or housing, and the specific requirements for the development. Start now ## What happens after you apply? Once your application has been submitted, the NHC will acknowledge receipt of your application. You should receive an acknowledgement letter within one week confirming that your application has been received and is being processed. Applications are maintained in the NHC database and are processed and assessed in accordance with the NHC policies and procedures. Eligible applicants will be submitted to the Board of Directors for consideration and approval when suitable land or properties becomes available. Applicants will be contacted regarding the outcome of their applications or when the appropriate property is available. ## Need assistance? If you are unable to apply online or require assistance completing the application form, please contact the National Housing Corporation. PBX: (246) 536-5300 Customer Service (Property Sales) Email: nhc.customerservice@barbados.gov.bb

pages.title: Apply to use state land
pages.description: Use this service to apply for permission to use land owned by the Government of Barbados for a specific purpose over a set period, such as an event, a project, or a community use.
pages.body_markdown: Use this service to apply for permission to use land owned by the Government of Barbados for a specific purpose over a set period, such as an event, a project, or a community use. ## Who can apply You can apply as an individual, a business, or on behalf of an organisation. ## Before you start You will need: - your National Registration Number (NRN) - the name of the organisation, if you are applying for one - your contact details: phone, email, and address - the **location of the land** you want to use, including the parish - the GPS coordinates of the land, if you have them, or a clear description of where it is - a **photo of the land**, if you have one - a clear description of **what you want to do** on the land, including the purpose and any structures or installations you plan to put there - the **start and end dates** you need the land for, and how long that is in days, months, or years You can upload the photo of the land as part of the form. ## When to apply Apply well in advance of the date you need the land. How long it takes to get a decision depends on how complex your request is and the checks the Ministry needs to do. ## Complete the form There are 2 ways to apply to use state land. You can: 1. ### Apply online You should complete your application in one go. At the moment, it is not possible to save your answers and come back to them later. Start now 2. ### Apply by email or by hand Contact the Ministry of Housing, Lands and Maintenance for the email address and office location. ## Cost There is no fee to apply. ## What happens after you apply You will get a confirmation email at the address you gave us. The Ministry of Housing, Lands and Maintenance will review your application and contact you using the details you gave. Your application may be turned down if your information is incomplete, the use you asked for is not approved, or the land is not available. If you are given permission and later need more time, you can ask the Ministry to extend your usage period. ## Contact If you have questions about your application, or you cannot apply online, contact the Ministry of Housing, Lands and Maintenance. If you need to change your application after you send it, contact the Ministry to ask for the change.

pages.body_markdown: If you rent a lot in a tenantry, the Tenantries Freehold Purchase Act (Cap. 239B) gives you the right to buy the freehold of that lot from your landlord. pages.title: Apply for financial assistance
pages.description: Apply for financial assistance from the Government of Barbados if you need help with food, clothing, utility bills, housing, assistive devices, or other essential needs.
pages.body_markdown:
If you live in Barbados and need financial help you can apply for financial assistance.

If you need help with things like food, clothing, burials, assistive devices (for example, dentures, hearing aids and spectacles), as well as payment of utility bills and house rent, you can apply for assistance in-kind.

A welfare officer will assess your needs under the National Assistance framework and make a recommendation to determine if you should be granted assistance.

## Who can use this service  

You can apply for assistance for a range of reasons, including if you:

- are unemployed or underemployed

- are elderly

- have a disability but are not receiving National Insurance and Social Security Service (NISS) benefits

- have children or dependents who you are struggling to support

- have finished school and are unemployed but have enrolled in a tertiary institution

- are homeless

- are the victim of a disaster or an accident

## How to apply for financial assitance

### Apply online or in person

You can apply for financial assistance either by:

1. Going to the welfare office in the parish where you live and completing a paper form (the National Assistance application form). At the moment, the form does not ask for your contact number but you must include one so an officer can reach you and arrange an interview.

Welfare offices  
Weymouth Corporate Center  
Roebuck St. Bridgetown  
St. Michael

Republic Bank Building,  
Chapel St,  
Speightstown,  
St. Peter

Country Road  
Bridgetown  
St. Michael

2. Completing the online form: [Application for National Assistance](https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=web15Rec90GA3HzH5NzlKVed1WgQV8FEk5jHDILeRuRUNTIzQ0QyODA2OEpTOUkyVzNVVEFWS1RJMi4u)  
   It will automatically be submitted to the department.

### What to bring

If you use the online form to apply, an officer will contact you and let you know how to share your supporting information.

If you apply in person, you will need to bring:

1. Your completed National Assistance application form.

2. Your national identification card. If you are applying on behalf of a child, you must also show their national identification card.

3. Bank or credit union details so financial support could be sent if you are eligible. (The electronic transfer of funds is not available yet but details are being taken in preparation).

4. Certificates or documents that are relevant to the assistance you are applying for.
   For example, proof of your income or unemployment, details of dependents, a medical form completed by your doctor, proof of your expenditure, for example, your utility bills.

If you are applying for health-related financial assistance, the welfare officer assigned to your case will issue you a medical form to take to your doctor to be completed.

### After you have applied

A welfare officer aims to complete their assessment within 6 weeks of receiving your application.

If you applied through the online form, they will let you know which supporting information they need, and where to send it.

The officer may ask you to take part in a phone or online interview, office interview or arrange a time for them to visit you at your home.

Following their investigation, the officer will compile a report on your circumstances and make a recommendation to a senior welfare officer to approve or reject the application. If they approve it, your bank information and the details of your payment will be forwarded to Accounts.

## No address and/or no bank account

If your application is approved and you do not live at a fixed address, you can make arrangements through the Post Office to receive your cheque. It is also possible to send cheques in care of a trusted friend or family member. The Department can also facilitate banking arrangements on your behalf.

## Reassessment and evaluation

Assistance is usually granted for 3 to 6 months. You can expect to have a review before the end of that period to determine whether an extension is needed. Welfare officers may ask to see your updated certificates and documents such as a more recent medical form or a letter from school which verifies the child is still in education.

## Get help with your application

If you want to apply but you cannot visit your local welfare office, and you cannot complete the form online either, contact:

Welfare Department  
Weymouth Corporate Centre  
Roebuck Street  
Bridgetown  
St. Michael

+1 246-535-1000/16/23

pages.title: Find out how much severance payment you are owed
pages.description: Estimate the severance payment you may be owed under the Severance Payments Act (Cap. 355A) if you were made redundant, your workplace was damaged by a disaster, you were laid off, or your employer died.
pages.body_markdown: If you were sent home from your job, your employer may owe you severance payment. This tool gives you an estimate based on the [Severance Payments Act (Cap. 355A)](https://www.nis.gov.bb/severance/) — it is not legal advice. You can use this tool if: - you worked for the same employer for at least **2 years** - you were between 16 and 67 years old on your last day at work - you were sent home because your job was cut, your workplace was damaged by a disaster, you had no work for a long time, or your employer died ## How to get your estimate ### Use the online calculator You will answer a short set of questions about why you were sent home, when you worked for the employer, and your usual gross pay. We then estimate how much you may be owed. Start your estimate now ## Do not wait too long You must make your claim within **12 months** of your last day at work. If you wait longer, you may lose your right to severance payment. ## Need help or advice? Contact the **NIS Severance Payment Department**. They can give you free advice and help you claim if your employer does not pay. NIS Severance Payment Department Frank Walcott Building Culloden Road St. Michael Phone: [+1 246-431-7400](tel:+12464317400), extensions 1502 to 1509
